cond_0001.intro:
We are looking for a Senior Education-Focused Quantitative Researcher to join our team.
[Company name masked] seeks a senior research and evaluation professional with expertise in analytical statistics, evaluation, and evaluation technical assistance to join our Research, Monitoring, & Evaluation Capability and play a leadership role on projects for the U.S. Department of Education (ED). As a member of the Research, Monitoring, and Evaluation Capability team, you will conduct research, monitoring, and evaluation services at the highest levels of quality and rigor to generate evidence-based insights.
The successful candidate will serve in such roles as Project Director, Principal Investigator, or Quality Reviewer on evaluation studies for ED and provide strategic expertise on education policy and ED-funded evaluation technical assistance contracts. The ideal candidate will have subject matter expertise in K-16 education, be highly knowledgeable about the What Works Clearinghouse Standards, and have significant experience working on ED/Institute for Education Sciences (IES) contracts.
cond_0001.responsibilities: Contribute subject matter expertise in K-16 education, including post-secondary pathways (career and technical education), student loans and loan repayment, Title IV, and the Every Student Succeeds Act (ESSA). Provide technical leadership on education evaluation strategies, design or execution of analyses (experimental, quasi-experimental, descriptive, and mixed-methods research), and other technical tasks (directing analyses, developing deliverables). Lead and mentor teams of experienced evaluators. Offer demonstrated experience with IES contract research that enables you to ensure project deliverables meet high IES client standards. Review, analyze, and synthesize information using appropriate practices and techniques and ensure that projects are conducted with sound practices and techniques. Work collaboratively as part of a team by communicating respectfully, meeting deadlines, and exercising initiative to resolve complex challenges. Develop guidance and deliver presentations on evaluation issues to audiences including federal grant program staff, IES, and evaluators. Represent [Company name masked] in a professional manner and effectively communicate with clients, external partners, and the public. Develop and disseminate project deliverables and other products to share project findings through papers, technical reports, client briefings, presentations, blog posts, podcasts, videos and/or social media. Lead business development activities including proposal writing and development. Cultivate and maintain excellent business development relationships with clients and external partners.
cond_0001.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Demonstrated technical expertise related to conducting rigorous evaluation of education programs and policies.
Exceptional quantitative skills with demonstrated technical expertise related to experimental and quasi-experimental designs for program evaluation in education.
Expertise in advanced statistical analysis and its applications in education research.
A record of publications, presentations, and other knowledge-dissemination activities.
Demonstrated experience translating research and making it accessible to practice, policy, and/or government audiences.
Demonstrated success with business development and proposal or grant writing.
A well-rounded interpersonal skill set with a demonstrated ability to build relationships with clients, funders, and education leaders, and to work effectively in a team environment.
Masters degree + 13 years of relevant experience, or PhD + 8 years of relevant experience.
Preferred Requirements
IES contract research experience.
In-depth knowledge of What Works Clearinghouse standards.
A collegial demeanor along with aptitude and interest in mentoring less-experienced staff and managing multidisciplinary teams.

cond_0149.intro:
We are looking for someone to join our team in this role.

The successful candidate will serve in such roles as Project Director, Principal Investigator, or Quality Reviewer on evaluation studies for ED and provide strategic expertise on education policy and ED-funded evaluation technical assistance contracts. As a member of the Research, Monitoring, and Evaluation Capability team, you will deliver research, monitoring, and evaluation services at the highest levels of quality and rigor to generate evidence-based insights.
The successful candidate will serve in such roles as Project Director, Principal Investigator, or Quality Reviewer on evaluation studies for ED and provide strategic expertise on education policy and ED-funded evaluation technical assistance contracts. The ideal candidate will have subject matter expertise in K-16 education, be highly knowledgeable about the What Works Clearinghouse Standards, and have significant experience working on ED/Institute for Education Sciences (IES) contracts.
cond_0215.responsibilities: Contribute subject matter expertise in K-16 education, including post-secondary pathways (career and technical education), student loans and loan repayment, Title IV, and the Every Student Succeeds Act (ESSA). Direct technical leadership on education evaluation strategies, design or execution of analyses (experimental, quasi-experimental, descriptive, and mixed-methods research), and other technical tasks (directing analyses, developing deliverables). Lead and mentor teams of experienced evaluators. Draw on demonstrated experience with IES contract research to ensure project deliverables meet high IES client standards. Review, analyze, and synthesize information using appropriate practices and techniques and ensure that projects are conducted with sound practices and techniques. Drive project outcomes by communicating respectfully, meeting deadlines, and taking initiative to resolve complex challenges. Develop guidance and deliver presentations on evaluation issues to audiences including federal grant program staff, IES, and evaluators. Represent [Company name masked] in a professional manner and effectively communicate with clients, external partners, and the public. Develop and disseminate project deliverables and other products to share project findings through papers, technical reports, client briefings, presentations, blog posts, podcasts, videos and/or social media. Lead business development activities including proposal writing and development. Cultivate and maintain excellent business development relationships with clients and external partners.
cond_0215.requirements: Demonstrated technical expertise related to conducting rigorous evaluation of education programs and policies. Preference given to those with IES contract research experience. Exceptional quantitative skills with demonstrated technical expertise related to experimental and quasi-experimental designs for program evaluation in education. Expertise in advanced statistical analysis and its applications in education research. In-depth knowledge of What Works Clearinghouse standards is a plus. A record of publications, presentations, and other knowledge-dissemination activities. A collegial demeanor along with aptitude and interest in mentoring less-experienced staff and managing multidisciplinary teams. Demonstrated experience translating research and making it accessible to practice, policy, and/or government audiences. Demonstrated success with business development and proposal or grant writing. A well-rounded interpersonal skill set with a demonstrated ability to build relationships with clients, funders, and education leaders, and to work effectively in a team environment. Masters degree + 13 years of relevant experience, or PhD + 8 years of relevant experience.
cond_0215.values: We value acting with integrity and keeping the interests of others in view. We aim to create positive outcomes through work that is respectful, fair, and responsible.

We are looking for a Senior Education-Focused Quantitative Researcher to join our team.
[Company name masked] seeks a senior research and evaluation professional with expertise in analytical statistics, evaluation, and evaluation technical assistance to join our Research, Monitoring, & Evaluation Capability. You will take a leadership role on projects for the U.S. Department of Education (ED) and regularly engage with clients, partners, and evaluation teams to generate evidence-based insights at the highest levels of quality and rigor.
The successful candidate will serve in roles such as Project Director, Principal Investigator, or Quality Reviewer on evaluation studies for ED, and will actively contribute strategic expertise on education policy and ED-funded evaluation technical assistance contracts. The ideal candidate will have subject matter expertise in K-16 education, be highly knowledgeable about the What Works Clearinghouse Standards, and have significant experience working on ED/Institute for Education Sciences (IES) contracts.
cond_0240.responsibilities:
Contribute subject matter expertise in K-16 education, including post-secondary pathways (career and technical education), student loans and loan repayment, Title IV, and the Every Student Succeeds Act (ESSA).
Provide technical leadership on education evaluation strategies, design or execution of analyses (experimental, quasi-experimental, descriptive, and mixed-methods research), and other technical tasks (directing analyses, developing deliverables).
Lead and mentor teams of experienced evaluators, staying in regular contact to guide their work and resolve challenges.
Draw on demonstrated experience with IES contract research to ensure project deliverables meet high IES client standards.
Review, analyze, and synthesize information using appropriate practices and techniques and ensure that projects are conducted with sound practices and techniques.
Work collaboratively as part of a team by communicating respectfully, meeting deadlines, and actively speaking up to resolve complex challenges.
Develop guidance and deliver presentations on evaluation issues to audiences including federal grant program staff, IES, and evaluators.
Represent [Company name masked] professionally and communicate directly and clearly with clients, external partners, and the public on an ongoing basis.
Develop and disseminate project deliverables and other products to share project findings through papers, technical reports, client briefings, presentations, blog posts, podcasts, videos and/or social media.
Lead business development activities including proposal writing and development.
Cultivate and maintain strong business development relationships with clients and external partners.
cond_0240.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Masters degree + 13 years of relevant experience, or PhD + 8 years of relevant experience.
Demonstrated technical expertise related to conducting rigorous evaluation of education programs and policies.
Exceptional quantitative skills with demonstrated technical expertise related to experimental and quasi-experimental designs for program evaluation in education.
Expertise in advanced statistical analysis and its applications in education research.
Demonstrated experience translating research and making it accessible to practice, policy, and/or government audiences.
A well-rounded interpersonal skill set with a demonstrated ability to build relationships with clients, funders, and education leaders, and to work effectively in a team environment.
Demonstrated success with business development and proposal or grant writing.
Preferred Requirements
IES contract research experience.
In-depth knowledge of What Works Clearinghouse standards.
A record of publications, presentations, and other knowledge-dissemination activities.
A collegial demeanor along with aptitude and interest in mentoring less-experienced staff and managing multidisciplinary teams.

cond_0519.intro:
[Company name masked] is looking for a senior research and evaluation professional with expertise in analytical statistics, evaluation, and evaluation technical assistance to join our Research, Monitoring, & Evaluation Capability. You will regularly work with teams and clients on projects for the U.S. Department of Education (ED), conducting research, monitoring, and evaluation services at the highest levels of quality and rigor to generate evidence-based insights.
You will serve in roles such as Project Director, Principal Investigator, or Quality Reviewer on evaluation studies for ED, and provide strategic expertise on education policy and ED-funded evaluation technical assistance contracts. The ideal candidate will have subject matter expertise in K-16 education, be highly knowledgeable about the What Works Clearinghouse Standards, and have significant experience working on ED/Institute for Education Sciences (IES) contracts.
cond_0519.responsibilities:
Contribute subject matter expertise in K-16 education, including post-secondary pathways (career and technical education), student loans and loan repayment, Title IV, and the Every Student Succeeds Act (ESSA).
Provide technical leadership on education evaluation strategies, design or execution of analyses (experimental, quasi-experimental, descriptive, and mixed-methods research), and other technical tasks (directing analyses, developing deliverables).
Lead and mentor teams of experienced evaluators, staying in regular contact to guide their work and resolve challenges.
Ensure project deliverables meet high IES client standards, drawing on your experience with IES contract research.
Review, analyze, and synthesize information using appropriate practices and techniques and ensure that projects are conducted with sound practices and techniques.
Actively contribute as part of a team by communicating respectfully, meeting deadlines, and speaking up to resolve complex challenges.
Develop guidance and deliver presentations on evaluation issues, directly engaging with audiences including federal grant program staff, IES, and evaluators.
Communicate with clients, external partners, and the public on behalf of [Company name masked] in a professional manner, walking them through findings and handling questions as they arise.
Develop and disseminate project deliverables and other products to share project findings through papers, technical reports, client briefings, presentations, blog posts, podcasts, videos and/or social media.
Lead business development activities including proposal writing and development.
Cultivate and maintain ongoing business development relationships with clients and external partners.
cond_0519.requirements:
Demonstrated technical expertise related to conducting rigorous evaluation of education programs and policies. Preference given to those with IES contract research experience.
Exceptional quantitative skills with demonstrated technical expertise related to experimental and quasi-experimental designs for program evaluation in education.
Expertise in advanced statistical analysis and its applications in education research.
In-depth knowledge of What Works Clearinghouse standards is a plus.
A record of publications, presentations, and other knowledge-dissemination activities.
A collegial demeanor along with aptitude and interest in mentoring less-experienced staff and managing multidisciplinary teams.
Demonstrated experience translating research and making it accessible to practice, policy, and/or government audiences.
Demonstrated success with business development and proposal or grant writing.
A well-rounded interpersonal skill set with a demonstrated ability to build relationships with clients, funders, and education leaders, and to work effectively in a team environment.
Masters degree + 13 years of relevant experience, or PhD + 8 years of relevant experience.

[Company name masked] seeks a senior research and evaluation professional with expertise in analytical statistics, evaluation, and evaluation technical assistance to join our Research, Monitoring, & Evaluation Capability and take a leadership role on projects for the U.S. Department of Education (ED). As a member of the Research, Monitoring, and Evaluation Capability team, you will conduct research, monitoring, and evaluation services at the highest levels of quality and rigor to generate evidence-based insights.
The successful candidate will serve in such roles as Project Director, Principal Investigator, or Quality Reviewer on evaluation studies for ED and provide strategic expertise on education policy and ED-funded evaluation technical assistance contracts. The ideal candidate will have subject matter expertise in K-16 education, be highly knowledgeable about the What Works Clearinghouse Standards, and have significant experience working on ED/Institute for Education Sciences (IES) contracts.
cond_0548.responsibilities: Bring subject matter expertise in K-16 education, including post-secondary pathways (career and technical education), student loans and loan repayment, Title IV, and the Every Student Succeeds Act (ESSA). Direct technical work on education evaluation strategies, design or execution of analyses (experimental, quasi-experimental, descriptive, and mixed-methods research), and other technical tasks (directing analyses, developing deliverables). Lead and mentor teams of experienced evaluators. Apply demonstrated experience with IES contract research to ensure project deliverables meet high IES client standards. Review, analyze, and synthesize information using appropriate practices and techniques and ensure that projects are conducted with sound practices and techniques. Take initiative to resolve complex challenges while communicating respectfully and meeting deadlines as part of a team. Develop guidance and deliver presentations on evaluation issues to audiences including federal grant program staff, IES, and evaluators. Represent [Company name masked] professionally and communicate effectively with clients, external partners, and the public. Produce and disseminate project deliverables and other products to share project findings through papers, technical reports, client briefings, presentations, blog posts, podcasts, videos and/or social media. Lead business development activities including proposal writing and development. Build and maintain strong business development relationships with clients and external partners.
cond_0548.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Demonstrated technical expertise related to conducting rigorous evaluation of education programs and policies.
Exceptional quantitative skills with demonstrated technical expertise related to experimental and quasi-experimental designs for program evaluation in education.
Expertise in advanced statistical analysis and its applications in education research.
A record of publications, presentations, and other knowledge-dissemination activities.
Demonstrated experience translating research and making it accessible to practice, policy, and/or government audiences.
Demonstrated success with business development and proposal or grant writing.
A well-rounded interpersonal skill set with a demonstrated ability to build relationships with clients, funders, and education leaders, and to work effectively in a team environment.
Masters degree + 13 years of relevant experience, or PhD + 8 years of relevant experience.
Preferred Requirements
IES contract research experience.
In-depth knowledge of What Works Clearinghouse standards.
A collegial demeanor along with aptitude and interest in mentoring less-experienced staff and managing multidisciplinary teams.

[Company name masked] seeks a senior research and evaluation professional with expertise in analytical statistics, evaluation, and evaluation technical assistance to join our Research, Monitoring, & Evaluation Capability and take a leadership role on projects for the U.S. Department of Education (ED). As a member of the Research, Monitoring, and Evaluation Capability team, you will conduct research, monitoring, and evaluation services at the highest levels of quality and rigor to generate evidence-based insights.
The successful candidate will serve in such roles as Project Director, Principal Investigator, or Quality Reviewer on evaluation studies for ED and provide strategic expertise on education policy and ED-funded evaluation technical assistance contracts. The ideal candidate will have subject matter expertise in K-16 education, be highly knowledgeable about the What Works Clearinghouse Standards, and have significant experience working on ED/Institute for Education Sciences (IES) contracts.
cond_0566.responsibilities: Bring subject matter expertise in K-16 education, including post-secondary pathways (career and technical education), student loans and loan repayment, Title IV, and the Every Student Succeeds Act (ESSA). Direct technical work on education evaluation strategies, design or execution of analyses (experimental, quasi-experimental, descriptive, and mixed-methods research), and other technical tasks (directing analyses, developing deliverables). Lead and mentor teams of experienced evaluators. Apply demonstrated experience with IES contract research to ensure project deliverables meet high IES client standards. Review, analyze, and synthesize information using appropriate practices and techniques and ensure that projects are conducted with sound practices and techniques. Take initiative to resolve complex challenges while communicating respectfully and meeting deadlines as part of a team. Develop guidance and deliver presentations on evaluation issues to audiences including federal grant program staff, IES, and evaluators. Represent [Company name masked] professionally and communicate effectively with clients, external partners, and the public. Produce and disseminate project deliverables and other products to share project findings through papers, technical reports, client briefings, presentations, blog posts, podcasts, videos and/or social media. Lead business development activities including proposal writing and development. Build and maintain strong business development relationships with clients and external partners.
cond_0566.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Demonstrated technical expertise related to conducting rigorous evaluation of education programs and policies.
Exceptional quantitative skills with demonstrated technical expertise related to experimental and quasi-experimental designs for program evaluation in education.
Expertise in advanced statistical analysis and its applications in education research.
A record of publications, presentations, and other knowledge-dissemination activities.
Demonstrated experience translating research and making it accessible to practice, policy, and/or government audiences.
Demonstrated success with business development and proposal or grant writing.
A well-rounded interpersonal skill set with a demonstrated ability to build relationships with clients, funders, and education leaders, and to work effectively in a team environment.
Masters degree + 13 years of relevant experience, or PhD + 8 years of relevant experience.
Preferred Requirements
IES contract research experience.
In-depth knowledge of What Works Clearinghouse standards.
A collegial demeanor along with aptitude and interest in mentoring less-experienced staff and managing multidisciplinary teams.

[Company name masked] seeks a senior research and evaluation professional with expertise in analytical statistics, evaluation, and evaluation technical assistance to join our Research, Monitoring, & Evaluation Capability and play a leadership role on projects for the U.S. Department of Education (ED). As a member of the Research, Monitoring, and Evaluation Capability team, you will conduct research, monitoring, and evaluation services at the highest levels of quality and rigor to generate evidence-based insights.
The successful candidate will serve in such roles as Project Director, Principal Investigator, or Quality Reviewer on evaluation studies for ED and provide strategic expertise on education policy and ED-funded evaluation technical assistance contracts. The ideal candidate will have subject matter expertise in K-16 education, be highly knowledgeable about the What Works Clearinghouse Standards, and have significant experience working on ED/Institute for Education Sciences (IES) contracts.
cond_0613.responsibilities: Contribute subject matter expertise in K-16 education, including post-secondary pathways (career and technical education), student loans and loan repayment, Title IV, and the Every Student Succeeds Act (ESSA). Provide technical leadership on education evaluation strategies, design or execution of analyses (experimental, quasi-experimental, descriptive, and mixed-methods research), and other technical tasks (directing analyses, developing deliverables). Lead and mentor teams of experienced evaluators. Offer demonstrated experience with IES contract research that enables you to ensure project deliverables meet high IES client standards. Review, analyze, and synthesize information using appropriate practices and techniques and ensure that projects are conducted with sound practices and techniques. Work collaboratively as part of a team by communicating respectfully, meeting deadlines, and exercising initiative to resolve complex challenges. Develop guidance and deliver presentations on evaluation issues to audiences including federal grant program staff, IES, and evaluators. Represent [Company name masked] in a professional manner and effectively communicate with clients, external partners, and the public. Develop and disseminate project deliverables and other products to share project findings through papers, technical reports, client briefings, presentations, blog posts, podcasts, videos and/or social media. Lead business development activities including proposal writing and development. Cultivate and maintain excellent business development relationships with clients and external partners.
cond_0613.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Demonstrated technical expertise related to conducting rigorous evaluation of education programs and policies.
Exceptional quantitative skills with demonstrated technical expertise related to experimental and quasi-experimental designs for program evaluation in education.
Expertise in advanced statistical analysis and its applications in education research.
A record of publications, presentations, and other knowledge-dissemination activities.
Demonstrated experience translating research and making it accessible to practice, policy, and/or government audiences.
Demonstrated success with business development and proposal or grant writing.
A well-rounded interpersonal skill set with a demonstrated ability to build relationships with clients, funders, and education leaders, and to work effectively in a team environment.
Masters degree + 13 years of relevant experience, or PhD + 8 years of relevant experience.
Preferred Requirements
IES contract research experience.
In-depth knowledge of What Works Clearinghouse standards.
A collegial demeanor along with aptitude and interest in mentoring less-experienced staff and managing multidisciplinary teams.
cond_0613.encouragement_text: Important: Even if you do not meet all of the qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply.

Master's degree in a relevant field or equivalent practical experience, plus around 13 years of relevant experience; or a PhD or equivalent practical experience, plus around 8 years of relevant experience.
Experience conducting rigorous evaluation of education programs and policies.
Working knowledge of quantitative methods, including experimental and quasi-experimental designs for program evaluation in education.
Familiarity with advanced statistical analysis and its applications in education research.
Experience translating research and making it accessible to practice, policy, and/or government audiences.
Experience with business development and proposal or grant writing.
Ability to communicate effectively and build relationships with clients, funders, and education leaders, and to work well in a team environment.
Openness to mentoring less-experienced staff and managing multidisciplinary teams.
Preferred Requirements
Experience with IES contract research.
Background in What Works Clearinghouse standards.
A record of publications, presentations, and other knowledge-dissemination activities.

cond_0634.intro:
We are looking for someone to join our team in this role.
[Company name masked] seeks a senior research and evaluation professional with expertise in analytical statistics, evaluation, and evaluation technical assistance to join our Research, Monitoring, & Evaluation Capability and play a leadership role on projects for the U.S. Department of Education (ED). As a member of the Research, Monitoring, and Evaluation Capability team, you will conduct research, monitoring, and evaluation services at the highest levels of quality and rigor to generate evidence-based insights.
The successful candidate will serve in such roles as Project Director, Principal Investigator, or Quality Reviewer on evaluation studies for ED and provide strategic expertise on education policy and ED-funded evaluation technical assistance contracts. The ideal candidate will have subject matter expertise in K-16 education, be highly knowledgeable about the What Works Clearinghouse Standards, and have significant experience working on ED/Institute for Education Sciences (IES) contracts.
People who do well in this role are often quick to grasp the logic of education evaluation methods and how they apply to policy questions.
cond_0634.responsibilities: Contribute subject matter expertise in K-16 education, including post-secondary pathways (career and technical education), student loans and loan repayment, Title IV, and the Every Student Succeeds Act (ESSA). Provide technical leadership on education evaluation strategies, design or execution of analyses (experimental, quasi-experimental, descriptive, and mixed-methods research), and other technical tasks (directing analyses, developing deliverables). Lead and mentor teams of experienced evaluators. Offer demonstrated experience with IES contract research that enables you to ensure project deliverables meet high IES client standards. Review, analyze, and synthesize information using appropriate practices and techniques and ensure that projects are conducted with sound practices and techniques. Work collaboratively as part of a team by communicating respectfully, meeting deadlines, and exercising initiative to resolve complex challenges. Develop guidance and deliver presentations on evaluation issues to audiences including federal grant program staff, IES, and evaluators. Represent [Company name masked] in a professional manner and effectively communicate with clients, external partners, and the public. Develop and disseminate project deliverables and other products to share project findings through papers, technical reports, client briefings, presentations, blog posts, podcasts, videos and/or social media. Lead business development activities including proposal writing and development. Cultivate and maintain excellent business development relationships with clients and external partners.
